extracted.intended_audience: design applicants, representatives (agents/attorneys), and national/regional IP Offices interacting with the Hague System
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, filing, managing and defending an international registration of industrial designs under the Hague Agreement (primarily the Geneva Act (1999)). Covers eligibility, required contents, fees, procedures before the International Bureau, publication, refusals, renewals, changes and notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement to file
rubrics_metrics.description: The entitlement to file an international application is limited to natural persons or legal entities having a real and effective industrial or commercial establishment, domicile, or habitual residence in at least one of the Contracting Parties, or being a national of one of these Contracting Parties, or of a member State of an intergovernmental organization that is a Contracting Party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 3. Check and document applicant’s entitlement (establishment, domicile, habitual residence or nationality) before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: No prior domestic application required
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of an international application does not require any prior domestic application or registration; protection may be applied for at international level for the first time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 5. An applicant may file directly at WIPO without national filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple designs per application (monoclass; max 100)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single international application may comprise several different designs, up to a maximum of 100; all designs included in the same application must belong to the same class of the Locarno classification (the application is 'monoclass').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 5; Rule 1(vi); Rule 7. Ensure all designs share same Locarno class and do not exceed 100 designs in one filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the international application
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application must contain, inter alia, a reproduction of the design concerned, together with the designation of the Contracting Parties in which protection is sought, and other prescribed items (see DM/1 items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 5; Rule 7. Provide clear reproductions, designate Contracting Parties, and complete all mandatory DM/1 items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages of filing
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application must be filed in English, French, or Spanish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 5; Rule 7. Choose one of the three accepted languages for form DM/1 or eHague filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of fees (basic, publication, designation fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application is subject to a basic fee, a publication fee and, for each designated Contracting Party, either a standard or an individual designation fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 7; Rule 12. Check Schedule of Fees and whether Contracting Party requires individual designation fees or standard fees (three-level structure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing channels: eHague or form DM/1
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application is normally filed directly with the International Bureau, either through the eHague Filing interface (recommended) or the official application form (DM/1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 4(1). Use eHague where possible; follow DM/1 item instructions when using form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination by the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt and payment of at least the basic fee for one design, the International Bureau checks compliance with prescribed formal requirements; the International Bureau does not examine novelty or substantive matters and cannot reject on substantive grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 14. Ensure formal requirements are satisfied because IB will only check formality, not novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication in the International Designs Bulletin (I.D.B.)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application that complies with formal requirements is recorded in the International Register and published in the I.D.B., a weekly electronic publication containing relevant data and reproductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 10(3); Rule 17. Publication normally occurs electronically on Fridays—be aware of publication cycle/timing provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination and possible refusal by designated Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication, each designated Contracting Party’s Office may carry out any substantive examination permitted under its law and may notify a refusal of protection for its territory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 12(1). Substantive refusals are handled by national Offices; IB does not assess substantive grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal time limits (6 months default; 12 months where declared)
rubrics_metrics.description: A refusal of protection must be notified to the International Bureau within six months from the date of publication; Contracting Parties that are Examining Offices or allow opposition may declare a 12-month refusal period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 12; Rule 18. Monitor refusal periods per designation and declarations in Member Profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic remedies for refusals
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of notification of a refusal, the holder has the same remedies as if they had filed directly with the domestic Office; appeals and contests proceed exclusively at domestic level according to that Contracting Party’s law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 12(3). Prepare to engage local counsel and follow domestic appeal/time limit rules if refusing Office notifies a refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of international registration as domestic grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a designated Office has not communicated a refusal (or has withdrawn it), the international registration produces the same effect as a grant of protection under the law of that Contracting Party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 14. The absence of a refusal within the period equates to domestic protection for that territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of grant of protection (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Office that has not communicated a refusal may send a statement that protection is granted; lack of such a statement has no legal consequence—the design is protected if no refusal was sent within the refusal period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 18bis(1). Do not rely solely on receiving a grant statement—verify the refusal period outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of protection and renewals (initial 5 years; renew 5-year periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: International registrations are valid for an initial period of five years and may be renewed for one or more additional periods of five years per designated Contracting Party, up to the maximum term provided under that Contracting Party’s law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 17. Check each designated Party’s maximum duration and renewal requirements; some Contracting Parties (e.g., certain Hague Act (1960) provisions) have specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum/mandatory declaration on maximum term of protection
rubrics_metrics.description: On acceding to the Geneva Act, a Contracting Party must notify the Director General of WIPO of the maximum duration of protection provided by its law and of any later amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 17(1),(2),(3)(c). IB uses this information in unofficial expiry notices sent to holders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes recordable in the International Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes that may be recorded include change in name/postal address of holder or representative, change in ownership (whole/partial), renunciation, limitation, and certain other changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 16(1); Rule 21. Use relevant official forms and pay prescribed fees (recording rep changes is free).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations by Contracting Parties (optional and mandatory declarations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Parties may make declarations affecting operation of the system (e.g., individual designation fees, refusal period extension, prohibition of filing through domestic Office, prohibition of self-designation, unity of design, requirement of certain views, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declarations list is available in Member Profiles on WIPO website. Consult declarations when choosing-designations or preparing application content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and consequences of an 'Examining Office'
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'Examining Office' is an Office which ex officio examines applications filed with it for protection of designs, at least to determine whether designs satisfy novelty; it must systematically carry out a prior art search matching the novelty criterion (worldwide search where required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geneva Act Article 1(xvii). Declarations and refusal periods may depend on Examining Office status—check Member Profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferment of publication (standard 30 months; shorter or none by declaration)
rubrics_metrics.description: General presumption permits deferment of publication for 30 months from filing (or priority) date; a Contracting Party acceding to the Geneva Act whose law allows less than 30 months may declare the shorter allowable deferment, or declare no deferment if law does not allow it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 16(1); 99 Article 11(1)(a),(b). Specify deferment needs and confirm effects on designated Contracting Parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of filing through domestic Office (declaration)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Contracting Party may declare that international applications may not be filed through its Office; when made, applicants attached to that Contracting Party must file directly with the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaration under Article 4(1)(b). Verify filing route constraints for an applicant’s Contracting Party before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of self-designation (declaration)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Contracting Party whose Office is an Examining Office may declare that its designation in an international application has no effect where it is the applicant’s Contracting Party (i.e., applicant cannot designate its own Contracting Party).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 4(1)(b); 99 Article 14(3). Check Member Profiles for such declarations when preparing designations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security clearance declaration (transmission period extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Contracting Party whose law requires security clearance may declare that the one-month period for its Office to transmit an international application to the IB is replaced by six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 13(4). Consider security clearance timing when selecting designations and expecting transmission to IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual designation fee: requirement, amount rules and payment in two parts
rubrics_metrics.description: A Contracting Party whose Office is an Examining Office may require an individual designation fee instead of a standard fee; the declaration must indicate the amount (currency) and may specify payment in two parts (first part at filing, second later). The individual fee must not exceed the equivalent amount the Office would receive for an equivalent domestic grant, reduced by international-procedure savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 7(2); Rule 12(3); Rule 28(2). For two-part fees (e.g., USA), second part may cover a 15-year duration; follow Rule 12(3) specifics and check currency conversions using UN rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of individual fees for Least Developed Countries (LDCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Contracting Party requiring individual designation fees is encouraged to reduce the fee to 10% of the fixed amount for applicants whose sole entitlement is a connection with an LDC or an intergovernmental organization whose majority members are LDCs (with related conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouraged by Hague Union Assembly; apply reductions where applicable and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard designation fee levels (level 1/2/3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard designation fees have three levels reflecting the scope of examination by an Office: level one automatically applies where Office does not carry out substantive examination; levels two or three apply where declared by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 12. Check whether a designated Office has declared level two/three and use Schedule of Fees to calculate amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing the international application form (DM/1) — Items 1–19
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guide provides detailed instructions for each DM/1 item (Item 1: Applicant; Item 2: Entitlement to file; Item 3: Applicant’s Contracting Party; Item 4: Email for multiple applicants; Item 5: Appointment of representative; Item 6: Number of designs/reproductions/specimens; Item 7: Designated Contracting Parties; Item 8: Product indication; Item 9: Description; Item 10: Legends; Item 11: Identity of the creator; Item 12: Claim; Item 13: Priority claim; Item 14: International exhibition; Item 15: Exception to lack of novelty; Item 16: Related designs/variants; Item 17: Publication of the international registration; Item 18: Reduction of the individual designation fee; Item 19: Signature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Guide's item-level instructions and the annexes (oath/declaration of creator, supporting documents). Use eHague assisted entry where possible to avoid errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claims and supporting documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority claims must be supported by a priority document; WIPO DAS and priority document procedures are available; annex lists supporting document requirements and how priority documents are handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide priority document or use WIPO DAS for electronic retrieval; Annex V and relevant A.I. sections explain required content and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproductions/specimens requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must include reproductions of the designs; the Guide includes presentation requirements for reproductions and specifications for views needed if declared by a Contracting Party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 7; Rule 9(3) where certain views are required by a designated Contracting Party. Ensure high-quality, clear reproductions and required views for targeted Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment, recording and effect of a representative
rubrics_metrics.description: A representative may be appointed by the applicant; the Guide specifies method of appointment, recording and notification, the legal effect of appointment, cancellation of recording, and that recording representative changes is free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow methods and forms specified in Guide and Administrative Instructions. Recording a representative is required for communications in some contexts—record promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of time limits and excuse of delay
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guide explains calculation of time limits for filings and communications and provisions for excuse of delay in meeting time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Guide sections on calculation of time limits and A.I. sections for excusing delay; do not rely on non-official notices as excuses for missing deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modalities of communications with the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guide covers permitted modalities (electronic, mail), official Hague System forms, channels of communication, and how communications are recorded and acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer eHague/electronic channels for speed and reduced errors; consult Guide for required forms and filing channels for specific actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment procedures and handling insufficient fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees must be paid to the International Bureau by required dates; if an amount received is insufficient, the IB notifies the holder/representative specifying the missing amount; insufficient payment after the six-month grace period results in non-recording and refund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 24(3); Rule 29. Use eHague fee calculator; if payment is insufficient, consider omitting certain designations or designs within the missing-payment time window to avoid lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal procedure and fees (eHague Renewal, components, partial renewal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal may be for all or only some designated Contracting Parties and/or designs; eHague Renewal is available and calculates renewal fees; renewal fees comprise a basic fee plus individual designation fees (where required) and standard designation fees for others; renewal may be paid up to six months late with surcharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 24(1); Rule 27(6)(b). Submit renewals before expiry or within six-month grace period (pay surcharge). eHague Renewal helps calculate and pay fees; partial renewals are possible using DM/4 or equivalent communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period for renewal and consequences of non-renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees should be paid by the expiry date but may be paid within six months after expiry provided the surcharge is paid; failure to renew results in lapse from expiry date and publication of non-renewal after possibility to renew has ended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 24(1)(c); Rule 26(1)(vii). Keep track of IB unofficial expiry notices but do not treat their absence as a valid excuse for missed payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording, publication and certificate of renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewals are recorded in the International Register (with the date on which they were due) and published in the I.D.B.; IB sends a certificate of renewal to the holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 25(1),(2); 99 Article 17(5). Expect formal confirmation once renewal is recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special renewal/payment rules for certain Contracting Parties (example: USA two-part fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Contracting Parties (e.g., United States) have special rules: the US individual designation fee is payable in two parts, the second part covering a single 15-year duration from date of grant; subject to payment of second part, no renewal is required to maintain effects in the US, though renewal can be paid to enable centralized recordal actions at IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 99 Article 7(2); Rule 12(3). Check country-specific declarations and fee rules—use fee calculator and country notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient fees at renewal: options and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If renewal payment is less than required, IB notifies missing amount; if missing amount is not corrected within six months (including surcharge), renewal is not recorded and IB refunds amount received; holder may instead request omission of some designated Contracting Parties/designs to reduce required amount if done within the allowed time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 24(3). Consider partial renewal or prompt payment of missing sum to avoid lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation in a designated Contracting Party
rubrics_metrics.description: Invalidation (revocation/cancellation) decisions are made by competent authorities of designated Contracting Parties under their domestic law; proceedings are between holder, third party and competent authority and may require local representation. When an invalidation is final, the Office must notify IB with specified data and IB records and publishes the invalidation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 20. Prepare to litigate/defend domestically and follow obligations for notification and recording once invalidation is final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irregularities in the international application
rubrics_metrics.description: IB may identify irregularities in the international application; the Guide includes procedures for irregularities, how they are notified and what corrective actions can be taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Chapter V and applicable Rules (e.g., Rule 14) for irregularity types and cure periods—use eHague to minimize irregularities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections in the International Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors or changes in the International Register can be corrected following specified procedures and forms; certain recordings (e.g., representative changes) are free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 21 and related A.I. sections. Ensure accuracy at filing to minimize later corrections; follow prescribed forms/process for corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing, cycles and deferment beyond standard period
rubrics_metrics.description: Guide explains publication cycles, timing of publication in the I.D.B., options for deferment of publication and requests to provide extracts or authorize access (including confidential copies to Examining Offices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 17; Rule 16. Use deferment options where secrecy or commercial reasons require delayed publication; be aware of procedures for granting Examining Offices access to confidential copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording of changes in ownership and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Change in ownership may be recorded in the International Register for all or some designated Contracting Parties and designs; procedures, contents of requests, possible refusals by designated Offices and effects of recordings are set out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 21; Chapter VI. Some Contracting Parties may refuse the effects of recording—check national law and ensure documents/supporting evidence are in order when requesting recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and recording of renunciation and limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Holder may renounce or limit designs in respect of some or all designated Contracting Parties; procedures, fees, irregular request handling and publication/recording rules apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to 'Renunciation' and 'Limitation' chapters—use official forms and pay fees; consequences depend on scope and postings in the I.D.B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional provisions for London Act (1934) and Hague Act (1960)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guide explains termination of the London Act and the freeze of the Hague Act (1960), and special transitional provisions that apply to designations under those Acts filed before their respective freeze/termination dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 37(2); 60 Article 6(4)(a). Check whether a given registration/designation is governed by older Acts and follow corresponding transitional rules for refusals, term calculation and recordings.
